title: 3 · Ram speed and strain-rate sensitivity
summary: Hot aluminium is rate sensitive: forge a flanged shaft slowly (hydraulic press) and fast (screw press).
instructions: 1. The flow stress follows σ̄ = C·(ε₀+ε̄)ⁿ·ε̄̇ᵐ with m ≈ 0.12 for 6061 at 450 °C.
2. Run its multi-run over ram speed 10 → 1000 mm/s (a factor of 100).
3. Expected: the load rises by about 100^m ≈ 1.7×. Check the ratio of the peak loads in RUNS.
4. Switch the field to Effective strain rate and compare a slow and a fast run: the pattern is the same, the magnitude scales with speed.
5. This model is isothermal. In reality a fast press also heats the part (deformation heat) and chills it less, which lowers the load again.
